newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway crown strengthens on C. Bank announcement.
newsitem.headline: Norway crown strengthens on C. Bank announcement.

text.p: The Norwegian crown rose on Tuesday following an announcement by the central bank, Norges Bank, that it was lifting a self-imposed curb on intervention in the foreign exchange market.
At 0735 GMT, the crown stood at 103.13 against the inverse European Currency Unit index and at 4.1970 against the mark, compared with 103.95 and 4.2310 respectively at 0630 GMT.
Market players said they had taken the bank's statement as a signal the bank now wanted to stabilise the exchange rate of the crown.
In January Norge Bank announced it would stop intervening on the forex market after massive and fruitless intervention failed to halt a strong appreciation of the petrocurrency.
But recently the crown has weakened considerably on higher-than-expected inflation figures for May, weaker oil prices and concerns over the outcome of parliamentary elections in September.
Harald Andreassen, chief economist at Oslo-based Elcon Securities said the bank's decision was "sensible" given the recent strong fluctuations in the crown's exchange rate.
"It's better to use intervention than interest rates to stabilise short-term swings in the market. This is a very sensible solution," Andreassen told Reuters.
He said he saw little chance of the bank raising interest rates in the near future.
"In order for them to do that (raise interest rates) what they are doing today wouldn't work, but we already see that it is working," he said.
